newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Traders welcome cut in Israeli interest rate.
newsitem.headline: Traders welcome cut in Israeli interest rate.

text.p: Traders in the stock market welcomed the 0.5 percentage point cut in the central bank's key lending rate but said it was expected and would not solve the problems of the stock market.

"Some business people will be disappointed because they were expecting a higher cut. But I think it was the right thing to do because inflation expectations have picked up. You've got to go gradually when you cut rates," said Gad Haker of Batucha Securities.

He said he expected trading to be positive, but mainly because of two or three stocks that would pull the market up. "Some people even believe the market will go down because some in the market expected a bigger cut in interest rates. Trading volumes are very low."

Dan Scharia of Capital Investments said it was difficult to predict how trading would go. "Volumes are very low. Yesterday volumes were only 45 million shekels. There are still many problems in the market. In principle the market will react positively to the interest cut."
Dan Propper, president of Israel's Manufacturers Association told Israel Radio that the rate cut was a small step in the right direction, but not enough.
